candidates.exact_span: Qa = critical low flow of the receiving waters (Qa = 0)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of whether Qa is truly zero (and thus CD = 100%) affects dilution/mixing assumptions used in reasonable-potential analysis, which can change which numeric discharge limits are derived as applicable.

A different reading of the dilution-credit fraction (CD) or the underlying formula inputs would change how effluent is credited against receiving-water criteria, affecting which enforceable numeric limits apply.

candidates.exact_span: The reasonable potential calculation was performed using test results for those parameters (tested at MQL) that were greater than the MQL. Detection limit values were used for those parameters reported as non-detect whose values are above the MQL.
candidates.computation_change_reason: How MQL thresholds and non-detect/detection-limit substitutions are applied in RP calculations determines which reported values count toward limit derivation and how censored results are treated for compliance comparison versus missing-evidence classification.

candidates.exact_span: For RP calculation purpose, averaged value of data set is utilized in the RP calculations.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether 'averaged value' means arithmetic mean, geometric mean, or another aggregate (the segment elsewhere cites geometric means for specific parameters) changes the concentration used in RP/limit derivation and thus which numeric limit is deemed applicable.

candidates.exact_span: effluent data for Total Recoverable Cyanide 6.28 ug/L (Estimated or J, 5/20/2020) and (ND < MDL of 2.96 ug/L, which was below the MQL of 10 ug/L, 5/26/21), and (ND <RDL of 0.005 mg/L), with a geometric mean of 2.854 ug/L
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of J-flagged estimates, non-detects below MQL versus RDL, and whether the geometric mean or individual sample values govern comparison can change both the applicable limit assessment for cyanide and the missing-evidence/no-result classification of individual measurements.

candidates.exact_span: The limiting Wildlife Habitat and Chronic Aquatic Criteria is 5.2 ug/L.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether this 5.2 ug/L wildlife-habitat/chronic criterion is an enforceable permit limit or only a background criterion used in RP analysis affects whether reported cyanide measurements have an applicable numeric compliance limit.

candidates.exact_span: As a result, the draft permit establishes monitoring requirements for Total Recoverable Cyanide to obtain more data for later RP analysis.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether cyanide is subject only to additional monitoring (not a numeric limit) versus an enforceable discharge limit determines applicable monitoring obligations for FY2025 and how absent or non-numeric cyanide results are classified (required monitoring vs. no numeric comparison applicable).

candidates.exact_span: NMWQS does not have numeric criteria for delta-BHC.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes that no state numeric water-quality criterion exists for delta-BHC; interpretation of whether any other derived or federal criterion nonetheless applies determines if an enforceable numeric discharge limit exists for this parameter.

candidates.exact_span: EPA proposes additional delta-BHC monitoring in the effluent to be used in the next permit cycle should there be sufficient toxicological studies at that time to calculate limitations.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether this language creates a present monitoring obligation or only contemplates future limit-setting affects which delta-BHC monitoring requirements are deemed applicable in FY2025 and whether missing delta-BHC results reflect required monitoring without adequate evidence.

candidates.exact_span: the permittee is required to submit a detailed plan to test for Delta-BHC at the source water intake within six months after the effective date of the permit to both EPA and NMED for approval.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of the six-month post-effective-date plan-submission requirement (and whether it was satisfied or is currently applicable) determines whether a delta-BHC source-intake testing plan obligation was in force during FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: Once approved, the permittee must collect and analyze samples for delta-BHC at least once a quarter or more frequent during the 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th year of the permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether FY2025 falls within the 2nd–5th permit years and whether plan approval triggered this quarterly sampling obligation determines applicable monitoring requirements and whether absent delta-BHC results represent missing required evidence versus periods when conditional monitoring was not yet required.

candidates.exact_span: The results of this study shall be attached to the DMR reports to EPA.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of this DMR-attachment requirement defines the expected reporting channel and frequency for delta-BHC study results, affecting whether monitoring was required to be documented on DMRs and whether missing DMR entries constitute inadequate evidence.
